scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The 1783 and 1938 imported footprints span approximately -78.979 to -72.737 longitude, 20.915 to 26.929 latitude. Extents support the shared archipelago identity but do not certify coastline or every island.

Lucayan archaeological traditions extend into Turks and Caicos, which are not silently equated with the modern Bahamas. Named object and household examples here concern Long Island, San Salvador and New Providence. First-arrival dates differ across studies; the opening phase is explicitly approximate.

The tourism history’s precise earliest dates, assertions of universal peacefulness, population totals, complete biological extinction and its 1649 colonization date are not adopted. Its limited 1718 and Loyalist account is used alongside plantation research.

Pottery and weave evidence is distinguished from experiment or interpretation. Adjacent Clifton sites are not automatically contemporary, and household activity areas are interpretations of artifact distributions.
Cat Island’s profile is a named family account. Bush teas are described as cultural practice without efficacy claims or instructions. No claim is made that all households share the practice.
The National Archives page erroneously describes the 1833 law as ending the slave trade, which had been prohibited earlier. Only abolition implementation and apprenticeship passages are used.

The postal-service commemoration supplies the 1967 coalition account; the simplified government timeline claiming a one-seat PLP electoral majority is not used. Voting rights, majority rule and independence remain separate phases.

Some government PDFs returned direct-access errors; their indexed passages supplied the stated claims. The independence brief is a British official account, not a complete account of everyone’s political views.
No quotations from songs, speculative remedies, invented successor links or exact coordinates for vulnerable archaeological finds are included. New text awaits independent review.

sharedAssociations.basis: Decoded 1783 and 1938 snapshots cover the same Bahamian archipelago. The shared geographic narrative distinguishes Lucayan communities, colonial institutions and the independent state.
